bullets.title: June FOMC delivers hawkish shock: 9 dots for hikes, core PCE revised to 3.3%
bullets.body: Nine of 18 FOMC participants penciled in at least one 2026 rate hike (6 see 2+ hikes, 1 sees 3); only 1 dot favors a cut. Core PCE forecast revised sharply higher to 3.3% for 2026 (from 2.7% in March), with return to 2% target pushed to late 2028. Fed Chair Warsh dropped forward guidance entirely, shortened the statement, and announced five reform task forces — a deliberate shift toward opacity. Markets now price ~36-40 bps of hikes through year-end vs. ~19 bps pre-meeting. MS and 22V believe the SEP overstates inflation risk (MS projects 3.0% core PCE) and forecast a hold through year-end, but JPM flags meaningful tightening risk if monthly core PCE stays above 0.21%; it is currently tracking ~0.36%.

bullets.title: US-Iran MOU signed; Strait of Hormuz reopening drives WTI -10% on the week
bullets.body: A US-Iran memorandum of understanding was signed, ending the conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz beginning Friday. WTI fell ~10% on the week to the low $70s; Goldman, BofA, and Citi cut 2026 Brent forecasts to ~$80. Stranded supply in the Gulf (80-90M+ barrels, per Jefferies estimates) is front-loaded, compressing prices faster than new production would. Wolfe and Piper flag Iran could add 4M+ bpd by 2027; long-dated WTI below $70 signals a durable headwind. Lower oil is disinflationary and supportive for consumer discretionary, travel, airlines, and housing — JPM flipped to Tactically Bullish on the risk-on impulse.

bullets.title: Semis/memory dominate weekly winners: WDC +32.6%, MU +15.5%, DRAM ASPs surging
bullets.body: WDC hit +32.6% on the week (+333% YTD) after Morgan Stanley raised PTs to WDC $650 / STX $1,035 on Asia checks showing nearline HDD price targets of $25-30/TB vs. current <$15/TB and supply-demand shortages extending through CY28. Citi raised MU PT to $1,200 on DRAM ASPs expected +200% in 2026, with spot prices already 52% above January and 21% above contract prices. Memory now represents 32% of HF leverage. MU reports June 24 AH with $20.57 EPS / $35.56B revenue consensus.

bullets.title: GS Prime: HF gross leverage near 4-year highs; positioning historically stretched, semi VaR risk flagged
bullets.body: Global fundamental L/S funds +15.4% YTD with +8.4% alpha. Net exposure rose +6.2 pts to 4-year highs (89th percentile 5-year). Semiconductor allocations more than doubled YTD to record highs; Mag7 net exposure at 1-year lows as shorts increase. US gross leverage fell 3.4 pts to 207.3% (4th percentile 1-year) but the L/S ratio hit a 98th percentile reading. JPM warns rising semiconductor stock volatility (market cap-to-revenue at 6x) poses a VaR-shock risk; estimated $165B of quarterly rebalancing selling is ahead. Semis gross leverage peaked around mid-June OPEX; seasonal decline typically follows.

bullets.title: AI capex cycle upgraded to $5.5T through 2030; MSFT faces $90-130B funding gap, AVGO backs $35B Anthropic order
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised total AI capex through 2030 to $5.5T (from $5.1T) with 138 GW data center capacity, debt financing at 85%+ LTC. GOOG and AMZN are aggressively pre-funding; MSFT is ~1 year behind the curve with a $90-130B FY27-28 gap, flagged as likely the largest new IG bond supply in 2H26. NVDA raised $20-25B in bonds. AVGO/Apollo/Blackstone backed a $35B Anthropic AI chip order. Agentic workloads now consume 23x more tokens than conversational tasks, driving Jevons dynamics despite cost pressure. AWS Bedrock AgentCore volume up 15x in 6 months.

bullets.title: ACN crashes 24.8% on week — AI disintermediation fears accelerate IT services derating
bullets.body: Accenture F3Q revenue of $18.72B slightly missed; FY26 CC growth guidance cut to 3-4% from 3-5%; managed services book-to-bill fell below 1.0x for the first time since 2019. The company announced ~$4.175B in cybersecurity acquisitions (Dragos, runZero, NetRise). Multiple analysts cut PTs and downgraded. The miss reinforced the narrative that AI is cannibalizing traditional consulting spend — software IGV was down 14.2% YTD and hit -2.57% on the week as ACN dragged IT services peers (CTSH, EPAM, INFY all fell).

bullets.title: FOXA-ROKU merger: Fox acquires Roku for $160/sh (~$22B); FOXA -17% on deal announcement
bullets.body: Fox agreed to acquire Roku for $160/share (60% cash, 40% stock), valuing the combined entity at ~$22B EV. Combined company becomes third-largest US TV player by viewing share. Fox projects $400M run-rate cost synergies and FCF accretion within two years. Deal expected to close H1 2027; Fox shareholders own ~73% pro forma. ROKU was downgraded to neutral/hold by 8+ analysts. Wolfe notes low competing-bid probability given management support. Strategically, deal shifts FOXA toward faster-growing streaming/CTV from ~65% linear to ~50% by 2030.

bullets.title: INTC +10% on Trump-AAPL chip partnership announcement; 18A-P enters risk production
bullets.body: Trump announced Apple agreed to work with Intel on domestic chip design and manufacturing. Intel simultaneously disclosed 18A-P entered risk production with 9% performance / 18% power improvement over 18A. Deal size estimated at ~$1-1.2B annually, or ~5% of TSMC's Apple business. AAPL confirmed unavoidable price increases driven by memory/storage costs (up 80-90% YTD; hyperscalers have locked ~50%+ of supply). JPM estimates iPhone 18 ASP increases of ~$50, not the $200+ implied by press reports. AAPL shares +2.4% on week.

bullets.title: S&P 500 up 0.9% on week (11th gain in 12); Nasdaq +2.4% led by semis; breadth remains narrow
bullets.body: Dow and Russell 2000 hit fresh record highs. The S&P 500 is within ~1.5% of its June 2 all-time high. Only ~30% of S&P stocks outperformed (3rd percentile breadth). Tech/semis drove the tape while software, energy, and staples lagged. Retail flows reached $7.9B with NVDA, GOOGL, MSFT, MU, TSLA the top buys. Wells Fargo raised its year-end S&P 500 target to 7,950; Piper Sandler models 8,450 at 21.5x $393 2027 EPS. JPM's bull case tilts to 8,000+ under Quality Growth / Tech leadership.

bullets.title: Enterprise AI adoption enters optimization phase; token spend discipline rising across hyperscalers and enterprises
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirm a shift from 'tokenmaxxing' to 'token minimizing': AT&T curtailed AI usage for employees, Walmart capped tools, Uber exhausted its full-year budget in 4 months, MSFT is evaluating DeepSeek for cheaper Copilot Cowork. Median AI spend is $11.38/month per employee but top 1% spends ~$7,500. MSFT moved Copilot to usage-based pricing. AWS Bedrock volume up 15x, but observability and governance bottlenecks are slowing enterprise production deployments. This favors AI infrastructure (DDOG, security plays) over pure model vendors.

bullets.title: BoJ hiked to 1% (31-year high); ECB expects one more hike; global central banks diverge post-Iran deal
bullets.body: Bank of Japan raised policy rate 25bps to 1.0% in a 7-1 vote, with next hike expected in October. BoE held 7-2 (two hawks dissented for 25bps); JPM pushed its BoE hike call to November from July after UK CPI surprised at 2.8% vs 3.3% expected. ECB expects one more hike in September despite Iran-deal-driven oil price declines. Norges Bank held but guided to a September hike. Riksbank call pushed to December. The global rate cycle is increasingly divergent, with Fed hawkishness offset by easing commodity pressures.

bullets.title: Ethernet backend switch market surges >100% YoY; CLS #1, NVDA losing share to CSCO
bullets.body: Citi reports Ethernet backend switch market grew >100% YoY to >$3.7B; InfiniBand >200% YoY to >$2B. 800G dominates ~80% of Ethernet revenue. Celestica holds >25% share (but down ~5pts YoY), the only vendor shipping early 1.6T volumes. NVDA fell to 24% share (down 6pts YoY). CSCO gained significantly (+8pts) to ~8% overall and ~13% within top 4 cloud customers — largely tied to Meta deployments. ANET gained modestly to 12%. 1.6T ramps 2H26 with Amazon/Google first, Meta in 1H27 via CPO.

bullets.title: FERC unanimously approves Trump data center grid interconnection plan; IPP/power stocks benefit
bullets.body: FERC voted unanimously to approve Trump's plan directing grids to allow AI data centers to connect in a timely and orderly manner, with 90-day approvals expedited. FERC also approved PJM's revised co-location tariff. PUCT approved a batch interconnection process for ERCOT with 35 GW baseload and 65 GW under study. These actions are key catalysts for IPPs like TLN, CEG, VST. TLN also completed its $3.45B PJM natural gas asset acquisition and was initiated Buy at Goldman (PT $499).

bullets.title: WFE cycle upgraded 21%→28% for 2026; AMAT/LRCX/KLAC PTs raised as AI drives multi-year capex
bullets.body: JPM raised 2026 WFE forecast from 21% to 28% YoY ($145B) and 2027 from 18% to 29% ($200B). Citi raised PTs: AMAT to $710, LRCX to $450, KLAC to $290, with a $250B bull case for 2028. Top 4 US hyperscalers are expected to increase capex 80% YoY in 2026. NVIDIA reduced HBM2 DRAM in Vera Rubin NVL72 by ~50% due to supply constraints, potentially creating $15-30B in NAND greenfield capex needs. ASML CEO bullish on AI cycle; 90-tool EUV guide may be a floor with potential upside to 110-120 units.

bullets.title: Consumer confidence recovering on gasoline price decline; May retail sales +6.9% beat, AI-sourced traffic surges
bullets.body: PSC Macro's daily confidence survey spiked as gasoline fell below $4/gallon — particularly benefiting low-end consumers. May retail sales printed +6.9% ex-auto, accelerating ~210bps sequentially; strong in sporting goods, electronics, building materials but weak in furniture and autos. Circana May data: units fell 1.5% despite +1.3% spend, with trade-down pronounced. Adobe data shows AI-sourced retail visits up 138% YoY, converting 54% better and generating 54% more value per visit than non-AI traffic.

bullets.title: UBS upgrades MSCI AC World to 1200; favors Semis/Tech Hardware, underweights Software/Online Advertising
bullets.body: UBS raised its MSCI AC World target to 1200 from 1120 following Middle East settlement. EM tops the regional scorecard; US overweight on earnings/economic momentum; Europe and Japan underweight. Within tech: Semis and Tech Hardware remain top-ranked by earnings momentum (3.3 std dev overbought but favored over Software). The ML model favors Telecoms/Retailing for upside. UBS flags Semis and Tech Hardware as most likely downside per ML model, cautioning on crowding. Most crowded sectors: Autos, Semis, Capital Goods.

bullets.title: Capital markets activity surging: IPOs +415% YoY, M&A +64% YoY in 2Q26 QTD
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Deal Dashboard shows equity issuance up 117% YoY in 2Q26 QTD (North America +234%), IPOs up 415% YoY, and annualized M&A volumes up 64% YoY, accelerating from 44% the prior week. Sponsor M&A flipped positive (+1% YoY vs -13% prior week). Completed M&A up 27% YoY. The SpaceX IPO (briefly surpassing MSFT and AMZN in valuation) and AI infrastructure financings are dominating capital markets flows.

bullets.title: China growth slowing below 4%; May retail sales -0.6% YoY — first decline since Dec 2022
bullets.body: China's May retail sales declined 0.6% YoY, the first sub-zero print since the COVID era, missing consensus (-0.2%). Fixed asset investment slowed; infrastructure investment growth collapsed to 0.6% YTD. Property sales fell double digits. JPM cut 2Q26 China GDP to 3.3% annualized with downside risks; growth expected to stabilize below 4% in 2H26. Consumer pessimism is rooted in labor market softness and property market stress, not oil prices. Fiscal stimulus unlikely to accelerate materially near-term.

bullets.title: HDD cycle extended through 2028: WDC/STX base-case FY28 EPS 70% above Street consensus
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Asia supply chain checks show nearline HDD demand growing 40-50% annually while supply grows 30-35%, with shortages extending through at least CY28. Customers are signing 5-year LTAs through 2032 with hyperscalers prioritizing storage over compute. Current nearline price is <$15/TB; vendors are targeting $25-30/TB over 2-3 years. STX is Morgan Stanley's 'Top Pick' given greater relative margin expansion potential. Both WDC and STX FY28 EPS are modeled ~70% above Street consensus in the bull case.
